2026-11-19.title: Thursday of the Thirty-third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: The Lamb who was slaughtered ransomed us for God
The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God
If you had only recognised the things that make for peace
2026-11-19.verse: As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying, “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.”
theo: In heaven no one is found worthy to open the sealed scroll of history, and John weeps. Then he is told: the Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered. He looks, and sees not a lion but “a Lamb standing as if it had been slaughtered”. Christ's victory is the victory of self-giving love. The heavenly court sings a new song: “by your blood you ransomed for God saints from every tribe and language and people and nation”.

On earth, the Lamb weeps. Coming down the Mount of Olives, Jesus sees Jerusalem and weeps over it: “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace!” He foresees its destruction (fulfilled in AD 70), “because you did not recognize the time of your visitation”. God's tears are not weakness; they are the grief of love refused. Today too he visits us; the question is whether we recognise him.

live: Look back over today: where did God visit you?

2026-11-19.prayer: Lamb of God, slain and risen, you ransomed us with your blood. You wept over Jerusalem; do not let me miss the time of your visitation. Teach me the things that make for peace. Amen.

quick: The Lion of Judah is a slaughtered Lamb.
His blood gathers one people from every nation.
Jesus weeps when his visit is not recognised.

2026-11-19.question: Did I recognise God's visit today?

homily: Dear friends, in heaven no one is found worthy to open the sealed scroll of history, and John weeps bitterly. Then he is told: the Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered. He looks, and sees not a lion but a Lamb standing as if it had been slaughtered (Revelation 5:5–6).

This is the surprise at the heart of our faith. Christ's victory is not the victory of force but of self-giving love. The heavenly court sings a new song: by your blood you ransomed for God saints from every tribe and language and people and nation (Revelation 5:9). Kerala, Vietnam, Germany, Italy: all are in that song.

In the Gospel, Jesus comes near Jerusalem, sees the city and weeps over it: if you had only recognised on this day the things that make for peace (Luke 19:42). God does not watch our wars and divisions coldly. He weeps over them.
The Lamb conquers by love, and he calls us to be people of peace. Pray for peace in the world each day this week, and make peace in your own home: one apology, one kind word, one forgiven hurt. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the Lamb of God who loves everyone in the world. He cried for his city because he wanted peace. Make peace with someone today!

intro: The slain Lamb conquers, ransoms every nation, and weeps over those who do not recognise his visit.

sub: No one could open the scroll.
The Lion is a slaughtered Lamb.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Singing with full voice, “Worthy is the Lamb that was slaughtered to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!”
points.apply: Pray the Agnus Dei slowly at Mass.

sub: His blood buys back all peoples.
The Church is catholic: from every tongue.
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.

They sing a new song: “You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slaughtered and by your blood you ransomed for God saints from every tribe and language and people and nation.”
points.apply: Pray for the Church in a country other than your own.

q: For these things I weep; my eyes flow with tears; for a comforter is far from me, one to revive my courage.
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying, “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.”
points.apply: Examine tonight where God visited you today.

concl: The Lamb conquers by love and weeps for us.
Recognise his visit and choose peace.
2026-11-19.resolve: Pray for peace in the world each day this week.
